meta.generatedFrom: TypeScript (the parity contract — never regenerate from Rust)
meta.description: nextInt(min, max) = min + (next() % (max - min + 1)). Outputs are recorded as f64 bits rather than JSON integers so the pathological cases (NaN) round-trip.
notes: The modulo is JS float remainder on a u32, which for a positive range equals u32 % range exactly.
Modulo bias is REAL and intentional here: ranges that are not powers of two (0..6, 0..9, 0..99) are slightly non-uniform, and a Rust port must reproduce the bias, not fix it.

`pathological` covers min > max. range == 0 yields NaN, range < 0 yields a remainder whose sign follows the dividend. A Rust `%` by zero PANICS, so the port must either mirror this or document that callers may not do it — the game never does.
meta.floatEncoding: bits = raw IEEE-754 f64, big-endian, 16 uppercase hex digits. dec = shortest round-trip decimal, informational only.
meta.nanPolicy: Every NaN is recorded as 7FF8000000000000 (the pattern of Rust f64::NAN). V8 does not emit a stable NaN sign/payload, so only NaN-ness is contractual — compare NaN results with is_nan(), not with bits.
